messages:
Taylor Kim: Morning pass-off — wanted to capture the tail of last night's 503 surge and what to watch for during my shift. INC-2026-045 is closed but there are follow-ups.

PagerBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered at 2026-03-12T23:42:11Z — high 5xx rate on /v1/generate for hosted-east-1. Severity: P2. Assigned to Ben Ortiz (primary).

Ben Ortiz: TL;DR — eviction thrash on dedicated pools caused a transient routing loop, ~12% of requests saw 500/503 for ~18m. We normalized by temporarily moving traffic to fallback pool and bumping reserved capacity + adjusted eviction cooldown.

Carla Nguyen: Notes from the replace deploy: we rolled a hotfix to eviction controller (reduced aggressiveness) and rolled back an experimental max-connections tweak. Logs look cleaner now. No customer escalations in the last 4h.

Dimitri Sokolov: Observability pointers — watch these dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/alerts/INC-2026-045 and the per-route latency heatmap. Key metrics to monitor: 5xx-rate, avg backend latency, kv-cache-hit-rate.

Taylor Kim: Current status — primary/secondary for next 12h: Ben (primary), Carla (secondary) until 17:00 UTC, then Dimitri takes primary at 17:00 UTC. Coverage gap: 02:00–03:00 UTC has no on-site coverage in APAC; flagged for escalation if pages occur then.

Ben Ortiz: Customer impact summary we posted to Ops notes: approx 12% of requests impacted, median latency bump from 220ms -> 1.4s during spike. Top affected customers: a small set of high-throughput tenants (internal IDs: CUST-311, CUST-489). No data loss, only increased errors and retries.

OpsRunbookBot: Runbook: Eviction-thrash mitigation — https://runbooks.redwood/internal/eviction-thrash. Quick steps: 1) route traffic to fallback pool, 2) increase reserved capacity, 3) set eviction cooldown to 90s, 4) monitor kv-cache regen.

Taylor Kim: Quick checklist I'm handing over (please ack):
- [ ] Confirm fallback pool routing is healthy (curl health endpoint on each host).
- [ ] Keep eviction cooldown at 90s for at least 6h.
- [ ] Monitor kv-cache-hit-rate for regressions.
- [ ] Post any customer escalations to #support-ops and tag @oncall.

Ben Ortiz: Acks — I did step 1 & 2. Routing checks:```
curl -sS https://host-fallback-1.internal/health | jq .status
# expected: "ok"
```

Carla Nguyen: Acknowledged. I left a small diagnostic gist with additional logs: https://gists.internal/eviction-logs-INC-2026-045 (includes `kubectl describe` output and eviction timestamps).

Dimitri Sokolov: Follow-ups I noted for longer-term work: tweak scheduler back-off heuristics, add circuit-breaker for eviction controller, and improve canary for eviction config changes. I'll open tickets: ENGINFRA-942 (scheduler tweaks), SERVE-776 (eviction circuit-breaker).

Taylor Kim: Next steps for the shift: Ben/Carla monitor the dashboards for 6h, if 5xx rate > 3% for >5m escalate to P1 and engage infra oncall. If we see kv-cache-hit-rate drop >15% post-fix, revert eviction controller fix and route traffic to warm pool.

Ben Ortiz: FYI — I ran a synthetic smoke test across routes (50 qps) and everything passed after the fix. Will keep test running at 5qps.

Carla Nguyen: Leaving notes on the runbook patch I started — adding a short diagnostic snippet to capture eviction timestamps and the relevant pod logs. Patch in PR: https://git.internal/runbooks/eviction/pull/12

Taylor Kim: Coverage reminder — APAC gap at 02:00–03:00 UTC: I've paged the on-call rotation owner to try and get backup coverage, but treat that time window as 'escalate to follow-up on-call' if anything happens.

Ben Ortiz: Adding final action items for whoever takes over: 1) Confirm reserved capacity autoscale policy didn't flip back, 2) check the canary config hasn't been auto-applied, 3) action security review if any customer raised data access concerns (none so far).

Dimitri Sokolov: I'll follow up with a short postmortem doc later today with timelines and root cause analysis. Expect draft by 13:00 UTC.

Taylor Kim: Thanks team. If no further comments, I'll close this pass-off in 15m. Please react with :white_check_mark: when you see this and are comfortable with items.

Ben Ortiz: :white_check_mark:

Carla Nguyen: :white_check_mark:

Dimitri Sokolov: :white_check_mark:

PagerBot: Note: No active pages in the last 10m.

Taylor Kim: Handoff complete.
